Usually one of the `crops` catalogue values (`Wheat`, `Barley`, `Canola`, `Maize`, `Sunflower`, `Peas`, `Grass`), but NOT guaranteed: `Parcel.cropType` is a free string and a spatial or cadastre import stamps whatever the source file carried. Label it the way the web does — `crops.<value>` when that key exists, the raw value otherwise, never hidden.

parcelCount.description: How many non-deleted parcels carry this crop, farm-wide across every block.

areaHaTotal.description: Total area in HECTARES, summed over those parcels. Null when none of them has a measured area — distinct from 0, which means measured and empty. Convert to дка for display; the server stores hectares.

ParcelCropTotal.description: One crop a farm grows, with its parcel count and area.

ParcelCropTotals.description: Every crop this farm grows. Parcels with NO crop are excluded — "no crop" is not an answer to "which crop did you treat", and such a parcel is still reachable through the per-block list.

areaHa.description: On-ellipsoid hectares, computed in PostGIS. A NUMBER here, unlike the STRING on an OperationParcel line.

coordinates.description: Nested coordinate arrays, as GeoJSON nests them — `[[[lon, lat], …]]` for a Polygon, one level deeper for a MultiPolygon. Left unconstrained here rather than modelled to four levels, which no generator handles usefully.

geometry.description:
GeoJSON geometry, WGS84. Simplified when the read passed `?simplify=` — never for sketch/edit, which needs exact geometry.

**Null is reachable and is not an error.** A simplify tolerance large enough to collapse a small parcel returns null rather than a degenerate shape, so a client must handle a parcel it cannot draw. Re-read without `?simplify=` to get the exact geometry.

cadastralId.description: КАИС identifier `ЕКАТТЕ.масив.парцел`; null when not linked.

soilType.description: Modelled soil label. Null while the async SoilGrids fetch is still pending.

absentFromImportAt.description: When the location’s LAST spatial import did not contain this parcel — it was kept, with all of its history, and marked. Null means it WAS in the last import, or that the location has never been imported into; both mean nothing to warn about. A TIMESTAMP rather than a boolean because "not in the last import" and "not in any import since March" are different facts and only the first is actionable — compare it against the location’s last import.

companyOwners.description: LEGAL-ENTITY owners from the КАИС register, joined at read time on `cadastralId`. Physical persons are never stored, so an individually-owned parcel has an EMPTY array — that is not "unknown owner".

hasActiveLease.description: A non-deleted lease with no end date, or an end date in the future.

ParcelGeo.description: A parcel as the map and the parcel list receive it — geometry as GeoJSON plus the soil and land-administration columns. Wider than the `Parcel` DTO, which describes the `LocationDetail` shape.

ParcelHistoryOperation.description:
A COMPLETED field-operation line for this parcel — the same rows that record a spray or fertiliser application, which is why "linked completed tasks" and "what was applied" are one list and not two. Pending lines are absent: a plan is not history. `doseValue` is a decimal STRING; parsing it as a float rounds the dose.

`title`, `productName` and `doseUnit` are EMPTY STRINGS when their source relation is absent, never null — empty means "not recorded", never "unknown". Filter them out of any concatenation rather than rendering a placeholder.

rentAmount.description: Decimal(14,2) → a JSON STRING, not a number. Parse it before arithmetic.

rentUnit.description: The CANONICAL unit the rent roll groups by — derived from what was sent, not the operator’s literal text.

rentUnitRaw.description: What the operator actually typed, verbatim.

ParcelLease.description: One land-use agreement (аренда/наем) over a parcel.

ParcelLeaseListResponse.description: Leases for one parcel, newest term first, capped at 100. Wrapped in `{ leases }` — the create and update return a BARE lease, unwrapped.

ParcelLeaseRequest.description: Create/update payload for a lease. The same schema serves both, so a PATCH is a FULL replacement: an omitted optional field is written as null, not left alone. Dates are loose strings parsed server-side; an unparseable one becomes null rather than a 400.

ParcelMergeRequest.description: Union ≥2 of the location’s parcels into one new parcel. The originals are SOFT-DELETED and their ids stop resolving — the response carries the new parcel only.

ParcelSplitRequest.description: A GeoJSON LineString blade. It must fully cross the parcel into ≥2 pieces or the request is a 400 and nothing changes.

ParcelSplitResult.description: The pieces the blade cut, each a brand-new parcel.

ParcelUpdateRequest.description: At least one field is required. Sending `geometry` RESHAPES the parcel (area is re-derived and a soil re-fetch is enqueued). Sending an empty `cadastralId` CLEARS the cadastral link; a malformed one is a 400.

ParcelUpdated.description: Area only. There is no `id` and no echoed parcel — re-read the parcel list if you need the updated row.

ParcelWeedObservation.description: `weedKeys` are catalogue Latin binomials and are the reportable half — group and count on these. `otherWeeds` is free text for a species the catalogue does not carry. Render them together; never merge them in storage.

cropType.description: The crop asked for, trimmed — echoed back so a client can match a response to a request.

ParcelsByCrop.description: The parcels of one crop, farm-wide.

expiresAt.description: When the invite stops appearing in this list. There is no `expired` state to observe — see the endpoint description.

PendingInvite.description: A pending invite. Deliberately carries NO acceptance token: the token is a bearer credential and belongs only in the `url` the create response returns (#1450).

PersonBlock.description: The person to block or unblock. The blocker is the authenticated caller and cannot be supplied.

notIncluded.description: Categories deliberately absent, in plain language, because Art 15 is a right to know what is held and a silent omission is a worse answer than a named one.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

contentReports.description: DSA Art 16 notices this person filed. RETAINED through erasure under Art 17(3)(b), which is what makes erasure incomplete — and why they are shown.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

statementsOfReasons.description: Art 17 statements addressed to this person. `actionId` is omitted, so nothing here reaches another party’s moderation record.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

blocksIMade.description: Social blocks this person MADE. Blocks against them are absent — a social block is silent in both directions by design.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

exchangeBlocksAgainstMe.description: Commercial blocks against this person. The OPPOSITE of a social block and included, because the exchange already discloses these to them live.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

exchangeListings.description: Listings this person created. The listing belongs to the farm; only the authorship column names them.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.
True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

exchangeInquiries.description: Enquiries this person made, including their own words.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

exchangeMessages.description: Messages this person SENT. A counterparty’s replies are somebody else’s words and are absent.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

insuranceLeads.description: Insurance quotes this person requested: the figures they supplied, and the premium they were quoted.

truncated.description: True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.
True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.
True when the 1000-row cap was reached, so rows may be missing. Said rather than silently returning a prefix.

featureCohorts.description: Dark-launch cohorts this person is in.

PersonalDataExport.description: Every collection is `{ rows, truncated }` and bounded at 1000. The collections present here are derived from one registry the ERASURE also reads, so a column exported but not erased — or erased but never shown — is not reachable.

Planting.description: One succession of a crop plan — the `plantingId` that yield records, cost entries and parcel history refer to. Generated from the plan rather than created directly; the only field a client may update is plannedYieldKgPerHa.

PlantingGdd.description: Growing-degree-day accumulation for one planting. totalGdd is 0 rather than null when there is no weather or no sow date, so a zero is not evidence of anything by itself — check sowDate. targetGdd null means no maturity percentage can be shown.

PlantingSoilSuitability.description: Soil-aware suitability for one planting, comparing the parcel’s modelled soil to the variety’s curated preferences. Advisory only.

PortfolioGrainSummary.description: Org-level grain portfolio rollup: contracted volume (sale/purchase), harvested yield, activity cost and bin storage aggregated across every child farm tenant, with org totals plus a per-tenant breakdown. Each per-tenant figure is computed inside an RLS-bound query against that tenant.

PracticeCreateRequest.description: Payload for creating a practice. Status defaults to NOT_STARTED. `code` carries the framework reference where one applies (e.g. ISO 27001:2022 A.5.1) and is minted as `CTL-N` for custom practices. Custom practices (isCustom=true) are tenant-specific.

cleared.description: FALSE when there was no live override, which is a 200 and not an error. A superuser clearing an override that was never set has the outcome they wanted, and a client retrying a clear is the normal case.

pointsWithdrawn.description: Points withdrawn from publication. They are NOT deleted — the series and its points are MARKED, so the typed history and the audit trail of what was typed both survive.

entryUnit.description: What to TYPE in, and what the POST will store the value under — `EUR/t` for the nine crops and fertilisers, `EUR/l` for diesel. Surfaced so a client does NOT hold its own copy of that split: the thing being duplicated is a UNIT, and a cross-repo copy has no guard that can see both sides. When two copies disagree the failure is not an error, it is a price wrong by 1000× that renders as a number.

typed.description: The CURRENT run only. `null` after a clear, even though the typed history is kept and the audit row for the clear carries it.

api.description: The feed’s current price, so the form can show what the override is replacing. A hand-entered `manual` price is NOT reported here: it is a typed price too, and presenting it as the API’s would say the override is replacing a feed when it is replacing somebody’s typing.

apiFeed.description: A DIFFERENT claim from `api`, and both are needed. `none` means no feed exists for this commodity EVER — so a typed price is the only source and clearing it leaves nothing, which a client should say before confirming. `api: null` with a real feed means the feed exists but has no current point. One empty column for both would tell the owner their override is replacing something when it is replacing nothing, and would read as a broken feed.

written.description: Points written. Equal to `prices.length` on success, by construction.

handle.description: The farm’s public address. Its page is at `/f/{handle}`.

score.description: Trigram similarity, 0–1. **Zero when browsing** — a request with no `q` has no ranking signal, so every score is 0 rather than a meaningless small number. Do not render it as a relevance percentage; it is a sort key.

QueueStatement.description: A DSA Art 17 statement of reasons, queued for delivery. Stored rendered because what was sent is a fact, and re-rendering later from a changed template would answer a different question.

anonymous.description: Whether the notifier gave an id. **Never which one** — `reporterUserId` is not returned. A moderator decides on the CONTENT, and knowing who reported it invites deciding on the reporter. This flag is returned because it changes whether there is anyone to answer to.

detail.description: The notifier’s own words, sanitised on the write path. `null` when they wrote nothing, or wrote only markup.

snapshot.description: Whether evidence was captured and, if not, why. `SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND` means the content was gone before the capture ran — the normal case for a notice about something real — and `SUBJECT_KIND_NOT_CAPTURABLE` means that surface has no capture path yet. The two are distinct so a deleted listing is not confused with a gap in our own code.

QueuedNotice.description: A notice as the triage queue shows it.

RawErrorResponse.description:
A bare error body: `{"error": "<code-or-message>"}` — NOT the `ErrorResponse` envelope, so there is no `code`, `requestId`, `details` or `params`. Used by the native auth family, where it is the shape RFC 6749 §5.2 specifies for an OAuth token endpoint, and by the cadastre-import job poll. The spatial-import routes used it until #1447 moved them to the envelope. A rate-limit (429) or an unexpected failure (5xx) on the same route still answers with `ErrorResponse`, because the error wrapper builds those rather than the route.

MOSTLY `error` alone, but not a guarantee: `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` adds `currentVersion` on its stale-version branch and declares that with its own `AcceptTermsErrorResponse`. This said "and nothing else" until #1478, which was overstated the day it was written.

kind.description: Spraying fills the ДНЕВНИК’s химични обработки table; fertilising fills торове. Each carries its own columns, which is why this is a kind rather than a free label.

occurredOn.description: The calendar DAY the treatment happened — a day, not an instant, because that is what the register records and what a farmer knows. It dates both the journal entries and the completed lines. **A future day is refused** (`TREATMENT_DATE_IN_FUTURE`), and a day that does not exist, such as 2026-02-31, is refused rather than rolled forward (`TREATMENT_DATE_INVALID`).

parcelIds.description: The parcels treated, as one flat list that may span blocks. The server groups them and writes one field operation per block — the ДНЕВНИК resolves a treatment’s block through the task’s location link, so a single task spanning blocks would print a parcel under a block it was never on. Empty is refused with `TREATMENT_NO_PARCELS`; a parcel of another farm with `REFERENCE_NOT_IN_TENANT` and `params.reference: parcels`, as a 400 rather than a 404 so the refusal does not confirm the row exists somewhere.

productName.description: A typed product name, resolved to the farm’s own product of that name or created. Send this OR `productItemId`.

pppRegistrationNo.description: ЗЗР рег. № — consulted only when a typed product name has to CREATE a product the farm does not have.

quarantinePeriodDays.description: Карантинен срок in days, AS IT APPLIED ON THE DAY. Stored on each line this treatment records (#1775), so a reprinted ДНЕВНИК shows the waiting period that applied then — and the «най-ранна дата за прибиране» computed from it — even after the product’s own period is later edited. Applies whether the product is one the farm already has or one this call creates; previously it reached only a newly created product’s registration and was dropped for a known product. Omit it and the line stores NULL, which means “not captured” and makes the register fall back to the product — never zero, which would print a waiting period nobody gave. When a typed `productName` has to CREATE a product it ALSO lands on that product’s registration; on a name that MATCHES an existing product the product is not rewritten, because an operation payload must not silently change a stored ЗЗР registration.

targetNote.description: Вредител — the pest or disease treated.

doseValue.description: Доза на приложение. Per-decare for the register; the unit says which.

applicationTechnique.description: Техника за приложение — one rig per treatment, as the field reality is.

RecordDiaryTreatment.description: A treatment a farmer already carried out. Recorded as DONE — handing work to an operator stays in Задачи.

treatmentGroupId.description: The treatment handle. Equals the `Idempotency-Key` you sent; a UUID minted by the server when you sent none.

parcelCount.description: Lines written across every block — the number to show the farmer.

taskIds.description: One per BLOCK, not per parcel. The register joins a block through the task’s location link, so a treatment spanning three blocks is three tasks.

replayed.description: True when this request resolved onto an existing treatment and wrote nothing.

RegisterStartResult.description: Intentionally carries no information about the address. Adding a field here that varied with account state would re-open the enumeration oracle this shape exists to close.

RentRoll.description: Rent by lessor with obligations and payments.

RestoredLogEntry.description: The entry as it is once restored.

RiskLevel.description: good | watch | stress | unknown. `unknown` means no usable satellite reading, not a failure — render it as absence, never as a fourth severity.

Season.description: A marketing/growing season — the `seasonId` that grain costs, yield records and contracts refer to. startDate and endDate come back as full instants even though they are written as calendar days.

SeasonRecap.description: A season’s headline figures. GROSS and moisture-standardised tonnage are both reported and are not interchangeable; costPerHa is null when nothing carried a cost, which a client must not render as zero.

body.description: The message text. **4000 is measured AFTER sanitising and trimming**, not on what the user typed: the server strips every tag, decodes the canonical entities, trims, and only then checks the length — so padding with markup cannot smuggle a longer message past the limit. **Capping at 4000 client-side is sufficient and conservative.** Sanitising only ever SHORTENS — tags are removed, and `<` becomes `<`, four units to one — so the sanitised length never exceeds the input length. A client that caps cannot be surprised by `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG`; that refusal is only reachable by a client that does not cap. The unit is **UTF-16 code units**, not characters and not bytes. For Cyrillic that is 1:1, so a Bulgarian farmer gets 4000 characters. Outside the BMP it is not: an emoji is 2 units, so 2001 emoji is refused at 4002. Counting grapheme clusters over-estimates the allowance; counting bytes under-estimates it. `minLength: 1` is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the surprising part: emptiness is judged after sanitising too. `` is eight characters, satisfies this constraint, sanitises to the empty string, and is refused with `MESSAGE_EMPTY`. A payload can pass the schema and still be rejected as empty. **The server's request validator deliberately permits more (8000).** That is not a contradiction and not a bug: Zod cannot sanitise, so it is a cheap outer bound that rejects absurd payloads, and the real gate is the usecase — which is what keeps `MESSAGE_TOO_LONG` reachable as a CODE rather than collapsing it into a generic validation error. 4000 is the limit a client must respect.

SoilProfile.description: A parcel’s modelled soil profile, fetched asynchronously — null upstream while the fetch is pending, which is an ordinary state rather than an error.

SoilSuitability.description: An ADVISORY verdict. `unknown` is returned whenever the variety has no curated preferences or the parcel has no soil yet — never a fabricated verdict, so a client must render unknown as unknown rather than as a neutral pass.

fileRecordId.description: The staged upload; becomes Location.spatialFileId on success.

SpatialImportAccepted.description: The upload was staged and the parse queued. It has NOT been parsed yet — the parcels are replaced by the worker, so poll the job before refreshing the map.

bounds.description: Bounding box as `[west, south, east, north]` — `[minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]`, **longitude first**, per GeoJSON and the reverse of the `lat, lon` a human quotes. WGS84 degrees, exactly four numbers. Null when the import produced no bounded geometry.

SpatialImportDetails.description: The `details` payload of a completed `spatial-import` job. parcelCount is matched + created — what the file contained. flagged counts existing parcels the file omitted, which were kept rather than deleted, so it is deliberately NOT part of parcelCount.

file.description: Shapefile `.zip`, `.kml`/`.kmz`, or `.geojson`/`.json`. The byte cap is enforced on the declared size BEFORE the body is buffered: 5 MB for a shapefile, 10 MB for KML/GeoJSON.

cropType.description: Default crop stamped on every imported parcel. Blank means "mixed / set later".

SpatialImportUpload.description: multipart/form-data body for a parcel-boundary import.

params.description: Values for the client to interpolate into its own translated message, keyed per `code` — e.g. `{ "max": 120 }` for `FARM_NAME_TOO_LONG`. Ids and quantities only: strings and numbers, never an object and never personal data. Absent for codes that need no values.

StaleDataError.description:
A 409 `STALE_DATA` from the optimistic lock. `error.details.currentVersion` carries the version the server holds — read it from `error.details`, NOT from the body root. A client that treats this as success loses the operator’s edit (#921/#922).

The code is named here because this response had the only 409 in the spec that did not name one (#1391). It explained the semantics and the field to read, and never wrote the literal a client switches on — so the only `code` value visible was this schema's inherited `example: "NOT_FOUND"`, which is a plausible thing to code against and wrong. Four sibling 409s already name theirs in prose exactly like this: see `FarmProfileStaleDataError`, `OperationParcelStaleDataError` and `ItemNameConflictError`.

SuccessResponse.description: Empty success envelope. Returned by mutation endpoints that have no resource to echo back (e.g. status changes, links, deletes).

reason.description:
Why. REQUIRED since #1667 — it becomes the `rationale` of the `ModerationAction` this route records, which is encrypted at rest and is what an Art 17 statement of reasons is composed from. A decision that withholds a farm from a person is not recordable without one.

It was optional and the text was DISCARDED: only `hasReason: true|false` reached the platform audit chain, under a comment correctly saying the rationale belongs on `ModerationAction.rationale` — a row this path never created.

SuspendAccount.description: The account to withhold access from, and WHY. Both required.

resolvedAt.description: **NEVER SENT — there is no such column.** Use `completedAt`. Documented in error; kept only because removing it is a breaking change requiring an API_VERSION bump, which a field that has never been produced does not warrant.

completedAt.description: When the task was completed. THIS is the field the server sends — `resolvedAt` above is documented in error and never arrives. Detail only: the list projection omits it.

key.description: Human-readable handle, e.g. `FT-102`. Present on BOTH the list and the detail — one of the few non-list-projection fields that is.

operationType.description: FIELD_OPERATION only: `SPRAY`, `FERTILIZE`, `SEED` or `OTHER`. Persisted so the БАБХ ДНЕВНИК generator can split химични обработки from торове without re-deriving from the title; legacy rows are null and fall back to a derive-from-title reader. Detail only.

applicationTechnique.description: FIELD_OPERATION only — «Техника за приложение», one rig per job. Detail only.

clientMutationId.description: Offline exactly-once handle. When a FIELD_OPERATION is created from a queued outbox the client's outbox-item id rides in as `Idempotency-Key`; a replayed write dedupes on (tenantId, clientMutationId) and returns the original task. Null for online creates. Detail only.

Task.description:
Unified work-item record covering audit findings, practice gaps, incidents, improvements, and ad-hoc tasks. The type field discriminates which UI surfaces this row appears in.

The full row. `GET /tasks` serves the narrower `TaskListItem`; `GET /tasks/{taskId}` serves `TaskDetail`, which is this plus its relations.

TaskAssignRequest.description: Reassign or unassign a task. Pass null to clear the assignee.

TaskCommentAddRequest.description: Append a comment to a task. body is sanitized server-side (rich-text allowlist) and encrypted at rest (Epic B field-encryption manifest).

TaskCreateRequest.description: Create a task (unified work-item type covering improvements and ad-hoc tasks). The type discriminator gates which UI surfaces this work item appears in.

resolvedAt.description: **NEVER SENT — there is no such column.** Use `completedAt`. Documented in error; kept only because removing it is a breaking change requiring an API_VERSION bump, which a field that has never been produced does not warrant.

completedAt.description: When the task was completed. THIS is the field the server sends — `resolvedAt` above is documented in error and never arrives. Detail only: the list projection omits it.

key.description: Human-readable handle, e.g. `FT-102`. Present on BOTH the list and the detail — one of the few non-list-projection fields that is.

operationType.description: FIELD_OPERATION only: `SPRAY`, `FERTILIZE`, `SEED` or `OTHER`. Persisted so the БАБХ ДНЕВНИК generator can split химични обработки from торове without re-deriving from the title; legacy rows are null and fall back to a derive-from-title reader. Detail only.

applicationTechnique.description: FIELD_OPERATION only — «Техника за приложение», one rig per job. Detail only.

clientMutationId.description: Offline exactly-once handle. When a FIELD_OPERATION is created from a queued outbox the client's outbox-item id rides in as `Idempotency-Key`; a replayed write dedupes on (tenantId, clientMutationId) and returns the original task. Null for online creates. Detail only.

links.description: Edges to other records, newest first. DETAIL ONLY. Also available on its own at `GET /tasks/{taskId}/links`.

watchers.description: DETAIL ONLY. Nothing renders a watcher on either client today — the native app shows `_count.watchers` alone.

_count.description: Relation counts, so a client can badge without fetching the collections. DETAIL ONLY.

label.description: `SLA Breached`, `Triage SLA Breached`, or EMPTY when neither — including for every terminal status. An empty string is the normal case, not a missing value.

sla.description: DERIVED per request from severity + createdAt + status, not a stored column, which is why it is on no model. Added by `getTask`, so DETAIL ONLY.

TaskDetail.description: The task detail. `Task` plus the relations `getById` includes and the `sla` `getTask` derives. `GET /tasks` serves `TaskListItem` instead.

TaskEvidenceLinkRequest.description: Attach a URL as evidence on a task. File uploads use the multipart /evidence/uploads endpoint with a taskId.

entityType.description: What the task is linked TO: `ASSET`, `EVIDENCE`, `FILE`, `LOCATION`, `PARCEL`, `EQUIPMENT` or `PLANTING`. A growing union — treat an unrecognised value as an opaque link rather than an error.

entityId.description: The linked row's id. An id ONLY — nothing about the entity is resolved here.

TaskLink.description: One edge from a task to another record. Ordered newest first.

TaskLinkAddRequest.description: Link a task to another domain entity. The relation field captures semantic intent for downstream traceability views.

key.description: Human-readable handle, e.g. `FT-102`. Present on BOTH the list and the detail — one of the few non-list-projection fields that is.

TaskListItem.description: One row of `GET /tasks`. A PROJECTION of `Task`, not the whole record — twelve fields, matching `taskListSelect`. Do not decode a list row as a detail row: `description`, `resolution`, `metadataJson`, `reviewer`, `createdBy` and the relations are absent here and present on `TaskDetail`.

name.description: The parcel name as the farmer wrote it. NOT unique — two parcels on one farm may share a name, which is why the response is ordered by name AND id.

geometry.description:
The outline as GeoJSON **MultiPolygon** in WGS84, simplified for display. Always MultiPolygon, never Polygon: the column is `geometry(MultiPolygon, 4326)` and every write path normalises to it, so a client needs no Polygon branch.

**`null` means the parcel has no outline** — a normal state, not an error. Keep the parcel and say it is not drawn rather than dropping it, or your count will disagree with the task. A parcel whose geometry COLLAPSES at the display tolerance falls back to its exact outline rather than arriving as null, so null means exactly one thing.

TaskParcel.description: A parcel linked to a task, for a display-only map. Deliberately status-free: per-parcel operation status lives on the field-operation detail route, so this shape means the same thing whatever the task type is.

TaskParcelsResponse.description: Wrapped in an object rather than returned as a bare array, so a count or a bounds can be added later without a breaking change. The sibling `/links` returns a bare array and is the route that now cannot grow.

TaskSetStatusRequest.description: Lifecycle transition for a task. resolution is required (by convention) when moving to RESOLVED/CLOSED to provide context for the audit trail.

TaskUpdateRequest.description: Partial update for a task. Status changes and assignment go through their own focused endpoints.

user.description: Deliberately NO email — see the DTO docblock.

version.description: Send this back verbatim as `termsVersion`. It is a DATE plus a `-draft` suffix while these terms are unreviewed, and the suffix is deliberate — a stored row reading `…-draft` can never be mistaken for acceptance of a reviewed document. Treat it as an opaque string: do not parse the date, and do not compare versions for ordering.

url.description: The page to show. RELATIVE by design — this product is served on more than one hostname, so an absolute URL would bake in an origin that is right for only one of them. Resolve it against the origin you called.

TermsInfo.description: Carries no body text: open `url` to show the document, so its own draft banner travels with it rather than being restated as a field here.

TraceLotNode.description: One lot in the genealogy graph, annotated with the fields it touched.

TraceLotResult.description: A lot’s provenance in both directions. ancestors and descendants are flat arrays; `edges` is what makes them a graph.

occurredOn.description: The day the work happened as the FARM sees it (`YYYY-MM-DD`, Europe/Sofia), not a UTC slice of `occurredAt`. For a free-hand entry typed between 00:00 and 03:00 in Sofia those two differ by a day.

parcelCount.description: 0 on an ordinary manual entry. The discriminator for "is this a treatment".

totalAreaHa.description: HECTARES, as stored. The web renders decares; the conversion belongs where the number is shown.

doseUnit.description: The unit SYMBOL, not its id.

quarantinePeriodDays.description: The line's own period, falling back to the product's.

earliestHarvestOn.description: Computed server-side from the period that applied ON THE DAY, so every client shows the same date and it matches the PDF. Null when no period was captured — never the treatment day itself, which would read as "harvest today".

parcelCount.description: Lines across every block — planned, not necessarily recorded.

completedCount.description: Of those, how many are DONE. A line gets its ДНЕВНИК entry when it is marked DONE, so this is how much of the treatment the register actually has.

occurredOn.description: The calendar DAY the treatment happened, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Null when nothing has been marked yet — an unmarked line has no date.

complete.description: True only when `completedCount === parcelCount` and at least one line exists. False means partly recorded: retry on the SAME handle and the write finishes the rest.

tags.description: The tags ACTUALLY APPLIED — sorted, de-duplicated, with unrecognised keys dropped. Compare it with what you sent: asking for two tags and getting one back is how you discover that a stored preference has been renamed away. An empty array means the feed is unfiltered.

q.description: The search term applied, or null.

nextCursor.description: Pass back verbatim as `?cursor=` for the next page; null at the end of the feed. OPAQUE — do not parse or construct one. A cursor the server no longer recognises (the 60-day retention deleted its article) is IGNORED and you get the first page, never an error.

TrendNewsResponse.description: The aggregated news feed, newest first. category, tags and q each echo the filter that produced this payload, so a client holding a page can tell a stale response from the one it asked for — which matters more, not less, now that there are three filters to reconcile.

TrendPayload.description: `daysAvailable` can be SMALLER than `daysRequested` — a young tenant has fewer days of history than you asked for. Plot the range you were given, not the one you requested: a chart that pads the difference with zeroes shows a collapse that never happened.

TrendPoint.description: One observation. `date` is a calendar day, not an instant. `count` appears only on listings-derived series, where it is the distinct-tenant sample size — its absence means the series is not sampled, not that the sample was zero.

TrendPricesResponse.description: Market price series for one commodity, grouped by source and region. Staleness is generatedAt minus a series’ lastObservedAt and must be computed against generatedAt rather than the device clock — the payload is cached for 6h and a rural device may be hours off.

source.description: Which feed the quotes came from, e.g. `ec` or `alpha-vantage`. Series from different sources are NOT interchangeable: they quote different stages in different currencies, which is why they arrive as separate series rather than merged.

region.description: A COUNTRY code, not a Bulgarian oblast. Production carries `BG`, `EL`, `RO`, `EU` and — for Alpha Vantage — `GLOBAL`. The oblast codes used by Борса and the parcel registry do not appear here.

stage.description:
The delivery point or market stage WITHIN the region — a feed's own vocabulary rather than ours, so treat it as an opaque label and do not parse it.

It is what distinguishes two series that otherwise look identical: for wheat, the nine Bulgarian delivery points disagree by tens of euros, so a chart that merged them on `(source, region)` alone would average unrelated markets. `region` + `stage` together identify a series.

`National average` is the figure the dashboard prefers, because a farm is not tied to one depot — but not every commodity has one. Wheat, maize and barley do; sunflower's only Bulgarian series is `FGATE`. **Null is normal**, not missing data.

TrendSeries.description: One price line, grouped by (source, region, **stage**) so a chart can split lines that differ in unit, currency or delivery point — BG wheat has nine delivery points whose prices differ by tens of euros per tonne, so two series sharing a source and region are routinely different lines — series are NOT comparable across those without conversion. lastObservedAt is the newest observation anywhere, which is what distinguishes a series reporting this week from one that stopped months ago; both otherwise present a points array whose last entry looks equally current.

Unit.description: A unit of measure from the GLOBAL seeded catalogue — not tenant-scoped, and there is no write path for it. `measure` constrains which units a dose may use; match on `key`, never on the localised `name`.

UnitRef.description: The unit reference embedded in a catalogue item — no `name`, no `createdAt`.

customRoleId.description: `null` UNASSIGNS the custom role. Omitting the field leaves it unchanged — the two are different.

UpdateFarmProfileRequest.description: MERGE SEMANTICS (#1176). Every field is optional and an ABSENT field is LEFT UNCHANGED — only an explicit `null` clears one, and a blank string clears one too. So `{"urn":"123"}` sets `urn` and touches nothing else. `grainProduced` follows the same rule: absent leaves the list alone, while `[]` or `null` clears it. This was NOT the behaviour before #1176, when an omitted field was nulled and a per-field PUT wiped the record — if you are reading a cached copy of this spec, check that it carries this sentence. A read-modify-write that sends all thirteen fields is still correct and is what the web admin page does; it is simply no longer required. Concurrency: send `If-Match: <version>` to get a precondition — a stale one is a 409 (see below). WITHOUT it, writes are last-write-wins per FIELD: merge semantics already means two admins editing DIFFERENT fields no longer clobber each other, so the precondition closes the narrower SAME-field race rather than the whole lost-update problem. A body that mentions NO field is a true no-op: nothing is written and the version does NOT move, so an empty PUT cannot manufacture a conflict for anyone else. `sizeHa` is a number, bounded at 1,000,000 and refused if negative — and null is not 0: a farm nobody has measured and a farm of zero hectares are different claims. `grainProduced` holds up to 50 strings of at most 120 characters; the server drops blanks and de-duplicates case-insensitively while PRESERVING ORDER, so re-read the response rather than keeping what you sent.

UserRef.description: User identity reference embedded inside other resources (id + display name + optional email).

UserRefShort.description: User identity reference without email — used in audit-log entries and other places where leaking the email would be inappropriate.

YieldRecord.description: Actual harvest production total. tPerHa is computed and not stored — from netTonnesStd when a standardised tonnage exists, otherwise grossTonnes; tPerHaBasis says which, so two t/ha figures are never compared across different bases. valuationNotes is encrypted at rest, returned decrypted, and is absent (not null) on list rows.

YieldRecordList.description: A capped page of yield records. When truncated is true rows were DROPPED, so any total computed from rows is wrong — use totalCount. Note that valuationNotes is absent from these rows by design.

get.description:
Returns a FLAT array by default. With `limit` or `cursor` it returns `{ rows, nextCursor }` and carries a weak ETag (honours `If-None-Match` with 304). With `deleted=true` it returns `{ entries }` and escalates to an admin check. Three bodies on one operation — a client must branch on the query it sent.

**The PAGINATED branch is the ДНЕВНИК and folds one row per treatment (#1740).** A treatment writes one `INPUT_APPLICATION` entry per line — twelve parcels in three blocks is twelve entries — and the register shows ONE row. Each row stays ENTRY-SHAPED, carrying `id`, `type` and `status` at the top level with the treatment detail in an added `treatment` object, so a client that decodes rows as entries keeps working and ignores the extra key. The `id` is a real entry id that `GET /journal/{id}` answers.

`treatment` carries `treatmentGroupId` (the handle), `occurredOn` as a DAY, `kind`, `productName`, `parcelCount`, `totalAreaHa`, `blockNames`, `doseValue` + `doseUnit`, `targetNote`, `applicationTechnique`, `quarantinePeriodDays` and a server-computed `earliestHarvestOn`. An entry belonging to no treatment folds to ITSELF and its `treatment.parcelCount` is 0 — one list, both kinds.

`earliestHarvestOn` is computed from the period captured ON THE DAY (#1775), falling back to the product for lines written before that was stored. Same resolution the ДНЕВНИК PDF uses, so the list and the document cannot disagree about the same number. Null when no period was captured — never the treatment day, which would read as “harvest today”.

**Ordered by `occurredAt` — the day the work HAPPENED — newest first, not by the day the row was typed** (owner ruling 2026-10-14; see #1771). So a back-dated treatment sorts to its own date rather than to the top. The `cursor` for this branch is opaque and encodes `(occurredAt, treatmentGroupId)`: a cursor naming a ROW cannot skip a folded treatment, and one that tried returned 3 treatments as 6 rows. Treat it as opaque and send back exactly what `nextCursor` gave you; a malformed cursor returns the FIRST page rather than a 400, so a stale bookmark is recoverable.

200.description:
Entries, in one of THREE shapes — the query decides which, and a client that assumes one reads an absent key from another as an empty list rather than as an error.

**Only the paged `{ rows, nextCursor }` shape carries `treatment`** — the folded ДНЕВНИК aggregate (#1832). The bare-array default and the `?deleted=` trash view return rows WITHOUT it, so a client that reads `treatment` must send `limit` to get the paged branch. On that branch the object is ALWAYS present, with `parcelCount: 0` on an ordinary manual entry rather than being absent, so `parcelCount > 0` is the discriminator for "this row stands for a treatment".

400.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session was refused.

403.description:
Signed in, but not permitted.

Four of these come from `src/middleware.ts` rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on EVERY route and are the ones worth switching on:

- `ADMIN_REQUIRED` — the route is admin-only and this role is not.
- `CSRF_BLOCKED` — a cross-site admin request. Retrying will not help; the request must originate from the app.
- `MFA_REQUIRED` — the session carries a pending MFA challenge. Complete it and retry; the credential is valid.
- `TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` — consent has not been recorded. `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` is the way out, and the session must be re-minted afterwards because `termsPending` is a JWT claim.

Each carries a `message`. Since #1677 the SERVER translates it, into the language on the signed-in person's profile (`User.uiLanguage`, default Bulgarian) — NOT negotiated from `Accept-Language`, which this API deliberately ignores. So `message` is safe to render to a user for any code that has a catalogue entry.

  The migration is INCOMPLETE and visibly so: a code with no entry yet keeps its English developer-facing sentence, unchanged. There is no flag telling the two apart, which is why switching on `code` and holding your own copy remains the robust choice — the server's `message` is then a better fallback than it used to be rather than something you depend on. Route-level 403s carry their own codes and are described on the operation that returns them.

One route-level code is described HERE rather than per-operation. MOST operations cannot return it — it is confined to the five capability families named below — but it means the same thing on each of them, and one of the five (`upload`) is gated at a choke point that many unrelated routes reach, so an exhaustive per-operation list would be the kind that is wrong by omission:

- `ACCOUNT_DELETION_PENDING` — this person asked to delete their account and is inside the 30-day grace period, so the account creates nothing new. It is NOT a moderator action and NOT a permission problem: do not offer an appeal. Reachable on any MUTATION outside `/api/auth/**` and `/api/account/**`, which stay open precisely so the way out stays open — `DELETE /api/account/deletion` cancels it, and the person recovers their account and their listings in full. Reads are unaffected, and `GET /api/account/export` keeps working, because a right of access does not lapse because a right of erasure was invoked.

- `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` — a payment on this tenant failed and the 14-day grace period has elapsed. It is NOT a quota or a plan ceiling: the plan is untouched and nothing was exceeded. The withheld capabilities are exactly `exchange`, `trends`, `task.create`, `upload` and `journal.create`; every other surface, including reading everything already recorded, is unaffected. post.summary: Record a treatment already carried out
post.description:
The two-step «Нов запис»: pick a crop, tick parcels, describe one treatment. Recorded as DONE and dated by `occurredOn` — handing work to an operator stays in Задачи.

Send `Idempotency-Key` ALWAYS, minted BEFORE the first attempt and reused on every retry. Here it is also the TREATMENT HANDLE, returned as `treatmentGroupId`: the per-block writes derive their own keys from it, so a replay resolves on the handle rather than on any one of them, and the handle is what later addresses this treatment.

**A reused key RESUMES an unfinished treatment and REPLAYS a finished one.** A replay (`replayed: true`) happens only when every line is already DONE. If the treatment is partly recorded — any failure during marking leaves it so — this request finishes the remaining blocks and lines and answers `replayed: false`. It is safe to re-send: each block carries a derived idempotency key, so an existing block is replayed rather than duplicated, and only lines still pending are marked.

**A reused key is never REFUSED, and the body is not compared** (owner ruling 2026-10-14). Reusing a key whose body differs returns the ORIGINAL treatment with `replayed: true` and writes nothing — the edit is silently not applied. So mint a NEW key the moment a field or the parcel set changes; the server cannot detect that you did not. This matches every other idempotent write in this API (journal entries, the cost batch, exchange messages), none of which compares a body, and it is stated here because the alternative — refusing the reuse — is what a client would reasonably assume.

`parcelIds` is ONE flat list that may span blocks — the server groups it and writes one field operation per block, because the register resolves a block through the task’s location link.

No stock is deducted. A treatment is a RECORD of what was applied, and deducting from a lot the farmer may never have tracked would make the inventory wrong in the name of making the diary right (owner ruling 2026-10-13).

Refusals, each a 400 carrying `error.code`: `TREATMENT_DATE_INVALID` (a day that does not exist — 2026-02-31 is refused, never rolled forward to 3 March), `TREATMENT_DATE_IN_FUTURE` (you cannot have sprayed tomorrow), `TREATMENT_NO_PARCELS` (an empty `parcelIds`), and `REFERENCE_NOT_IN_TENANT` with `params.reference` naming which list held the stranger — a 400 rather than a 404 so the refusal does not confirm the row exists on some other farm. `params.reference` is `parcels` and nothing else on this route.

A treatment day is the FARM’s day (Europe/Sofia), not the server’s UTC day, so recording today keeps working after local midnight.

`PRODUCT_IS_SAMPLE_ARCHETYPE` — the chosen `productItemId` or `fertilizerItemId` is a SAMPLE product, not a registered one, and the farm record needs a trade name. Refused BEFORE anything is written, so nothing is left behind: the underlying operation write refuses a sample only on the way to DONE, which would leave a partial treatment whose cause repeats on every retry — unfinishable and, with no delete-by-handle yet, unabandonable. Reachable only by id; a typed product NAME never resolves to a sample.

Inherited from the operation write underneath, all 400: `OPERATION_INPUT_AMBIGUOUS` (not exactly one input kind, or an id AND a name for the same kind), `PRODUCT_DOSE_REQUIRED` / `FERTILIZER_DOSE_REQUIRED`, `PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` / `FERTILIZER_NOT_FOUND`, `PRODUCT_NAME_REQUIRED` (a name empty once trimmed), `FERTILIZER_EXPECTED` (the fertiliser field was given an item that is not a `FERTILIZER`; **the converse is deliberately NOT enforced** — a liquid fertiliser through a sprayer is a legitimate SPRAY, so the product field accepts any category), `PESTICIDE_REGULATORY_FIELDS_REQUIRED` (a typed name has to CREATE a plant protection product and the ЗЗР registration number or quarantine period is missing — `params.missing` names which), and `DOSE_UNIT_HAS_NO_BASE` (a typed name has to create a product but the dose unit is not a `<base>-per-<area>` rate, so no stock unit can be derived — create the product from the catalogue instead).

Recording a treatment needs WRITE. The restricted machine-operator persona (`MECHANISATOR`) does not have it and is refused 403 — by design: completing work handed to an operator stays in Задачи, and filling in the register is not an operator action.

get.description:
Answers whether a treatment was recorded under this handle, and in what state.

**This exists because the write replays a reused key without comparing the body.** A save whose response is lost, followed by an edit, goes out under a NEW key and writes a SECOND treatment if the first had landed. Asking whether the earlier handle exists is the only way a client can tell, so read this before re-sending an edited treatment under a fresh key.

Three answers, and a client needs all three:

| answer | meaning | what to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `404` `TREATMENT_NOT_FOUND` | nothing landed | write afresh |
| `200` `complete: true` | fully recorded | do not write again |
| `200` `complete: false` | PARTLY recorded — see `completedCount` | retry on the SAME handle; the write finishes the rest |

**`complete` counts DONE lines, not lines.** A line is created pending and marked DONE afterwards, and the mark is what writes the ДНЕВНИК entry — so a treatment whose lines all exist but are unmarked is in the register nowhere. Any failure during marking leaves earlier blocks recorded and later ones not, which is the partial state this answer exists for.

Treating it as a 404 writes a duplicate treatment; treating it as an ordinary 200 reports a compliance record the register does not have.

The handle is a PATH segment and not a query parameter on purpose: iOS writes the full URL including the query string to the device log, unsuppressably.

delete.description:
The other exit from a treatment that cannot be finished (#1777).

The write is resumable rather than atomic: re-sending the same handle finishes a partly-recorded treatment. That has one dead end — if the cause of the failure REPEATS, every retry fails identically and the farmer is left with a treatment that will neither complete nor go away. This clears it.

| `409` `TREATMENT_COMPLETE` | fully recorded, so it is a farm record — remove it through the journal, where a delete is reversible and separately audited |

Afterwards the handle stops resolving and is RELEASED: sending it again mints a new treatment rather than resuming the abandoned one. Unfinished lines move to `SKIPPED` rather than being deleted, because `OperationParcel` has no soft-delete column and the completion pass already refuses to touch that state.

get.description:
The Приложение 1 document limited to ONE treatment, across every block it touched: the farm header, a field header strip for each TREATED parcel, and only this treatment’s rows. Produced by the same gatherer and the same renderer as the per-block register, so the layout is identical and the document can be certified.

**Bytes inline.** 200 `application/pdf` with a `Content-Disposition` filename — no job, no URL to poll, nothing persisted. Check for `%PDF` and open it.

A GET where its per-block sibling is a POST, because the handle is this document’s only input and there is nothing to send. The handle is a PATH segment rather than a query parameter: iOS writes the full URL including the query string to the device log, unsuppressably.

The farm header’s block line is EMPTY, deliberately. A treatment spans blocks, so there is no one block to head the document with, and each field strip names its own — which is where the paper form puts it. Printing the first of several would be wrong and would look right.

Node runtime, 60s budget.

400.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session was refused.

403.description:
Signed in, but not permitted.

Four of these come from `src/middleware.ts` rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on EVERY route and are the ones worth switching on:

- `ADMIN_REQUIRED` — the route is admin-only and this role is not.
- `CSRF_BLOCKED` — a cross-site admin request. Retrying will not help; the request must originate from the app.
- `MFA_REQUIRED` — the session carries a pending MFA challenge. Complete it and retry; the credential is valid.
- `TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` — consent has not been recorded. `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` is the way out, and the session must be re-minted afterwards because `termsPending` is a JWT claim.

Each carries a `message`. Since #1677 the SERVER translates it, into the language on the signed-in person's profile (`User.uiLanguage`, default Bulgarian) — NOT negotiated from `Accept-Language`, which this API deliberately ignores. So `message` is safe to render to a user for any code that has a catalogue entry.

  The migration is INCOMPLETE and visibly so: a code with no entry yet keeps its English developer-facing sentence, unchanged. There is no flag telling the two apart, which is why switching on `code` and holding your own copy remains the robust choice — the server's `message` is then a better fallback than it used to be rather than something you depend on. Route-level 403s carry their own codes and are described on the operation that returns them.

One route-level code is described HERE rather than per-operation. MOST operations cannot return it — it is confined to the five capability families named below — but it means the same thing on each of them, and one of the five (`upload`) is gated at a choke point that many unrelated routes reach, so an exhaustive per-operation list would be the kind that is wrong by omission:

- `ACCOUNT_DELETION_PENDING` — this person asked to delete their account and is inside the 30-day grace period, so the account creates nothing new. It is NOT a moderator action and NOT a permission problem: do not offer an appeal. Reachable on any MUTATION outside `/api/auth/**` and `/api/account/**`, which stay open precisely so the way out stays open — `DELETE /api/account/deletion` cancels it, and the person recovers their account and their listings in full. Reads are unaffected, and `GET /api/account/export` keeps working, because a right of access does not lapse because a right of erasure was invoked.

- `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` — a payment on this tenant failed and the 14-day grace period has elapsed. It is NOT a quota or a plan ceiling: the plan is untouched and nothing was exceeded. The withheld capabilities are exactly `exchange`, `trends`, `task.create`, `upload` and `journal.create`; every other surface, including reading everything already recorded, is unaffected. The tenant's own ACTIVE exchange listings stay visible to other farms and inbound threads keep arriving — this is the unpaid tenant's own view closing, not a withdrawal.

  The restriction is COMPUTED per request, with no sweep and nothing to settle, so a cleared balance lifts it on the very next request — a client can honestly tell the user to resolve it and refresh. This description deliberately names no remedy beyond that: App Store guideline 3.1.1 keeps the native client from pointing anyone to pay outside the app, so a prescribed destination would be unreachable for one of the two clients (#1490). What both clients CAN do is distinguish this from `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and say which happened.

Five billing and capability codes are described here for the same reason and with the same caveat: each is confined to the routes that reach one gate, those gates sit below many operations, and an exhaustive per-operation list would be wrong by omission. Each carries `params` so a client composes its own sentence rather than rendering ours (#1679):

- `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — a per-plan ceiling on a COUNT was reached. Params: `plan`, `resource`, `limit`, `current`. Reachable wherever `assertWithinLimit` guards a create. It is NOT a payment problem and NOT a permission shortfall: nothing failed and no role lifts it. The remedy is a higher plan or deleting something, and this description names no destination for the same reason `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` does not.
- `AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` — the tenant has spent its monthly AI token budget. Params: `plan`, `limit`, `used`. It resets at the start of the next **UTC** month with nothing to settle, so a client can honestly say "next month" — which is what distinguishes it from the one above, where waiting changes nothing. UTC is stated because it is not local: for a Bulgarian user the reset lands at 02:00 or 03:00 on the 1st (EET/EEST), so copy naming a DAY would be wrong for a few hours each month. Raised by agrent-ios, which got this right before the spec said it.
- `AI_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` — the requested model TIER is above this plan's ceiling. Params: `plan`, `tier`, `ceiling`. Distinct from the budget code on purpose: the refusal is on capability, not on spend, so retrying at `ceiling` succeeds immediately and retrying the same tier never will.
- `MODULE_DISABLED` — a product module is off for this tenant. Params: `module` and `reason`. AVAILABLE is a conjunction (plan-allowed AND tenant-enabled) and `reason` says which half failed, because the remedies differ: `"tenant"` means an administrator of THIS farm can turn it on, `"plan"` means the plan does not include it and no administrator can. Do NOT name an administrator without reading `reason` — telling somebody to ask an admin who cannot help is the defect agrent-ios#241 is about, and an earlier draft of this paragraph said exactly that. A client that ignores `reason` should stay neutral; the code alone only means "off".
- `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — this deployment runs self-hosted and exposes no in-app checkout at all. Params: `mode`. Nothing the client or the user can do lifts it; do not offer a retry or a plan picker.

  TWO of the five are TRANSLATED by the server (#1677) — `MODULE_DISABLED` and `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — so their `message` is renderable to a user. The other three still carry an English developer-facing sentence: their Bulgarian needs ICU plural agreement, which the server-side renderer does not yet do, and shipping copy that interpolated a wire identifier (`exchange_listing`, `deep`, `FREE`) into a farmer's screen would have been worse than the English. They are tracked on #1677.

  All five carried a legacy `lower_snake:` prefix at the start of `message` until #1677; that prefix is GONE for all of them. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec and your client matches on `plan_limit_exceeded:` or a sibling, switch to `code` — the prefix was removed once the only client depending on it had shipped the codes.

One PERMISSION code is described here, and it is the most diffuse of all of them — 106 call sites, under most mutating operations in this document:

- `WRITE_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role in THIS farm may not modify records. Params: `role`. It refuses exactly three of the six roles — READER, MECHANISATOR and AUDITOR — and no other condition produces it: it is NOT a plan ceiling, NOT a payment problem, and NOT a moderator action, so retrying, paying or waiting all change nothing.   Uncoded until #1767, which is why a client reading a cached copy of this spec should treat its absence as "this server predates the code" rather than "this server cannot refuse a write".

Two more are described here rather than per-operation, and their scope is NARROWER than the four above: they come from `getUserCtx`, so they are reachable on the PERSON-scoped routes only — `/api/account/**`, `/api/me/**` and `/api/social/**`. - `API_KEY_NOT_PERSON_SCOPED` — an `iflk_` API key was presented on a route about a PERSON. - `OPERATOR_SCOPE` — the signed-in user is a MECHANISATOR and the route is a social surface. Deliberately narrower than the Edge lockdown of the same persona: an operator reaches their own account and security pages normally, because a lockdown that locks somebody out of their own credentials is a defect (owner ruling, 2026-10-02). Nothing the client can do lifts it; do not offer a retry.

Both carried their code in `error.message` with a generic `error.code` until #1645. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec, check that it carries this sentence before switching on either.

404.description:
Not found, or not visible to this tenant.

- `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` — no such farm, OR a farm this caller may not see, OR one removed from the organisation. X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Always `0` on a 429 — present for symmetry with the other headers.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time in SECONDS at which the window frees up.

**The FileRecord SURVIVES.** Detaching unlinks; it does not delete. A photo taken in a field and attached to a legally-filed record is evidence, and removing it from one entry is not a reason to destroy it.

schema.description: The file to unlink from this entry.

patch.summary: Mark one prescription line DONE / SKIPPED / PENDING
patch.description:
The write the offline outbox replays, so treat `If-Match: <version>` (digits only) as mandatory: it is what stops a queued mark clobbering a supervisor’s later edit. An absent or non-integer `If-Match` SKIPS the version check entirely — a silent last-write-wins, not an error.

A stale version has TWO possible answers, and telling them apart is the point. If the line already carries the status this write wanted, the intent is satisfied: 200 with `alreadyApplied: true`, the current `version`, and `resolved: false`. Otherwise 409 `STALE_DATA`. Answering a replay of the operator’s own success with a 409 asks them to resolve keep-mine versus take-server against themselves, which is not a question anyone can answer.

Authorisation is unusual here: the ASSIGNED operator may mark their own job even without general write permission. PATCH is the only method — there is no PUT alias, and no way to add a line to an existing job.

post.summary: Approve a field operation, or send it back
post.description: ADMIN-gated separation of duties: the operator marks the parcels, a reviewer finalises. Only a task in PENDING_REVIEW can be reviewed — any other status is a 400, not a 409, so a client must not retry it as a conflict. Notifies the assigned operator when there is one.

400.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

401.description: Not signed in, or the session was refused.

403.description:
Signed in, but not permitted.

Four of these come from `src/middleware.ts` rather than from any handler, so they are reachable on EVERY route and are the ones worth switching on:

- `ADMIN_REQUIRED` — the route is admin-only and this role is not.
- `CSRF_BLOCKED` — a cross-site admin request. Retrying will not help; the request must originate from the app.
- `MFA_REQUIRED` — the session carries a pending MFA challenge. Complete it and retry; the credential is valid.
- `TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` — consent has not been recorded. `POST /api/auth/accept-terms` is the way out, and the session must be re-minted afterwards because `termsPending` is a JWT claim.

Each carries a `message`. Since #1677 the SERVER translates it, into the language on the signed-in person's profile (`User.uiLanguage`, default Bulgarian) — NOT negotiated from `Accept-Language`, which this API deliberately ignores. So `message` is safe to render to a user for any code that has a catalogue entry.

  The migration is INCOMPLETE and visibly so: a code with no entry yet keeps its English developer-facing sentence, unchanged. There is no flag telling the two apart, which is why switching on `code` and holding your own copy remains the robust choice — the server's `message` is then a better fallback than it used to be rather than something you depend on. Route-level 403s carry their own codes and are described on the operation that returns them.

One route-level code is described HERE rather than per-operation. MOST operations cannot return it — it is confined to the five capability families named below — but it means the same thing on each of them, and one of the five (`upload`) is gated at a choke point that many unrelated routes reach, so an exhaustive per-operation list would be the kind that is wrong by omission:

- `ACCOUNT_DELETION_PENDING` — this person asked to delete their account and is inside the 30-day grace period, so the account creates nothing new. It is NOT a moderator action and NOT a permission problem: do not offer an appeal. Reachable on any MUTATION outside `/api/auth/**` and `/api/account/**`, which stay open precisely so the way out stays open — `DELETE /api/account/deletion` cancels it, and the person recovers their account and their listings in full. Reads are unaffected, and `GET /api/account/export` keeps working, because a right of access does not lapse because a right of erasure was invoked.

- `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` — a payment on this tenant failed and the 14-day grace period has elapsed. It is NOT a quota or a plan ceiling: the plan is untouched and nothing was exceeded. The withheld capabilities are exactly `exchange`, `trends`, `task.create`, `upload` and `journal.create`; every other surface, including reading everything already recorded, is unaffected. The tenant's own ACTIVE exchange listings stay visible to other farms and inbound threads keep arriving — this is the unpaid tenant's own view closing, not a withdrawal.

  The restriction is COMPUTED per request, with no sweep and nothing to settle, so a cleared balance lifts it on the very next request — a client can honestly tell the user to resolve it and refresh. This description deliberately names no remedy beyond that: App Store guideline 3.1.1 keeps the native client from pointing anyone to pay outside the app, so a prescribed destination would be unreachable for one of the two clients (#1490). What both clients CAN do is distinguish this from `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and say which happened.

Five billing and capability codes are described here for the same reason and with the same caveat: each is confined to the routes that reach one gate, those gates sit below many operations, and an exhaustive per-operation list would be wrong by omission. Each carries `params` so a client composes its own sentence rather than rendering ours (#1679):

- `PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — a per-plan ceiling on a COUNT was reached. Params: `plan`, `resource`, `limit`, `current`. Reachable wherever `assertWithinLimit` guards a create. It is NOT a payment problem and NOT a permission shortfall: nothing failed and no role lifts it. The remedy is a higher plan or deleting something, and this description names no destination for the same reason `PAST_DUE_RESTRICTED` does not.
- `AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` — the tenant has spent its monthly AI token budget. Params: `plan`, `limit`, `used`. It resets at the start of the next **UTC** month with nothing to settle, so a client can honestly say "next month" — which is what distinguishes it from the one above, where waiting changes nothing. UTC is stated because it is not local: for a Bulgarian user the reset lands at 02:00 or 03:00 on the 1st (EET/EEST), so copy naming a DAY would be wrong for a few hours each month. Raised by agrent-ios, which got this right before the spec said it.
- `AI_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` — the requested model TIER is above this plan's ceiling. Params: `plan`, `tier`, `ceiling`. Distinct from the budget code on purpose: the refusal is on capability, not on spend, so retrying at `ceiling` succeeds immediately and retrying the same tier never will.
- `MODULE_DISABLED` — a product module is off for this tenant. Params: `module` and `reason`. AVAILABLE is a conjunction (plan-allowed AND tenant-enabled) and `reason` says which half failed, because the remedies differ: `"tenant"` means an administrator of THIS farm can turn it on, `"plan"` means the plan does not include it and no administrator can. Do NOT name an administrator without reading `reason` — telling somebody to ask an admin who cannot help is the defect agrent-ios#241 is about, and an earlier draft of this paragraph said exactly that. A client that ignores `reason` should stay neutral; the code alone only means "off".
- `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — this deployment runs self-hosted and exposes no in-app checkout at all. Params: `mode`. Nothing the client or the user can do lifts it; do not offer a retry or a plan picker.

  TWO of the five are TRANSLATED by the server (#1677) — `MODULE_DISABLED` and `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` — so their `message` is renderable to a user. The other three still carry an English developer-facing sentence: their Bulgarian needs ICU plural agreement, which the server-side renderer does not yet do, and shipping copy that interpolated a wire identifier (`exchange_listing`, `deep`, `FREE`) into a farmer's screen would have been worse than the English. They are tracked on #1677.

  All five carried a legacy `lower_snake:` prefix at the start of `message` until #1677; that prefix is GONE for all of them. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec and your client matches on `plan_limit_exceeded:` or a sibling, switch to `code` — the prefix was removed once the only client depending on it had shipped the codes.

One PERMISSION code is described here, and it is the most diffuse of all of them — 106 call sites, under most mutating operations in this document:

- `WRITE_FORBIDDEN_FOR_ROLE` — the caller's role in THIS farm may not modify records. Params: `role`. It refuses exactly three of the six roles — READER, MECHANISATOR and AUDITOR — and no other condition produces it: it is NOT a plan ceiling, NOT a payment problem, and NOT a moderator action, so retrying, paying or waiting all change nothing. The remedy is a different role, which only an administrator of that farm can grant, and `params.role` is there so a client can name the role the person actually holds rather than guessing.

  Distinguish it from `ADMIN_REQUIRED` above, which comes from the Edge and means the ROUTE is admin-only. This one comes from a usecase and means the OPERATION needs write. A role can pass the Edge and still meet this.

  Uncoded until #1767, which is why a client reading a cached copy of this spec should treat its absence as "this server predates the code" rather than "this server cannot refuse a write".

Two more are described here rather than per-operation, and their scope is NARROWER than the four above: they come from `getUserCtx`, so they are reachable on the PERSON-scoped routes only — `/api/account/**`, `/api/me/**` and `/api/social/**`. No tenant route can answer either. They are here because that one function is the choke point all of those routes reach and three of their paths are not in this document yet, so a per-operation list would be wrong by omission:

- `API_KEY_NOT_PERSON_SCOPED` — an `iflk_` API key was presented on a route about a PERSON. Use a user session or a bearer token minted for one.
- `OPERATOR_SCOPE` — the signed-in user is a MECHANISATOR and the route is a social surface. Deliberately narrower than the Edge lockdown of the same persona: an operator reaches their own account and security pages normally, because a lockdown that locks somebody out of their own credentials is a defect (owner ruling, 2026-10-02). Nothing the client can do lifts it; do not offer a retry.

Both carried their code in `error.message` with a generic `error.code` until #1645. If you are reading a cached copy of this spec, check that it carries this sentence before switching on either.

TWO answers behind one path, chosen by `crop`. **Without it** you get the farm’s crops with parcel counts and total hectares, and no geometry — a crop picker draws nothing. **With it** you get that crop’s parcels, each carrying the block it sits in and a simplified outline for a map beside the list.

Before it existed a client had to fan out one request per block and group them itself.

Order is `name`, then `id`. The id tiebreak is contractual (#1391): parcel names are not unique, so without it a capped read could return a different subset between requests with nothing changed.

post.description:
This is where a field operation is created — there is no POST under `/field-operations`. Exactly ONE input: a product OR a fertilizer, never both and never neither, and the chosen kind’s dose and unit are then required.

Send `Idempotency-Key` — the outbox replays a queued job with its item id, and the usecase returns the original instead of a duplicate. The replay check requires `parcelCount > 0` on the existing job, because the create spans TWO transactions and a crash between them leaves a Task with no lines that must NOT be reported as synced.

**400 codes for the input a job applies.** `OPERATION_INPUT_AMBIGUOUS` — not exactly one kind, or an id AND a name for the same kind. `PRODUCT_DOSE_REQUIRED` / `FERTILIZER_DOSE_REQUIRED` — the chosen kind needs its dose and unit. `PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` / `FERTILIZER_NOT_FOUND` — the id names nothing in this farm. `FERTILIZER_EXPECTED` — the fertiliser field was given an item that is not a `FERTILIZER`. **The converse is deliberately NOT enforced**: a liquid fertiliser applied through a sprayer is a legitimate SPRAY, so the product field accepts any category. `PRODUCT_NAME_REQUIRED` — a `productName` empty once trimmed and sanitised. `PESTICIDE_REGULATORY_FIELDS_REQUIRED` — a typed name has to CREATE a plant protection product and `newProductRegistration` is missing a field, named in `params.missing`. `DOSE_UNIT_HAS_NO_BASE` — a typed name has to create a product but the dose unit is not a `<base>-per-<area>` rate, so no stock unit can be derived; create the product from the catalogue instead.

post.description:
ONE 200 with TWO media types, chosen by the `save` flag in the body. Default (`save` absent or false) → `application/pdf` bytes with `Content-Disposition: attachment`. `save: true` → `application/json` `{ fileRecordId, fileName }`, with the PDF filed in the register instead. Negotiate on what you SENT; an `Accept` header has no effect.

Read-only data, authorised by `assertCanRead` inside the generator. Runs on the Node runtime with a 60s budget.
